note: This particular accepted run used --heal-steps 0 (no healing), so it predates the sequential-heal restructure in behavior (schema fields renamed for consistency with later runs — same real numbers, not re-measured). heal_steps_per_layer=0 means heal_by_layer.layer0.losses is empty by construction, not a failure.
scope_note: Accepted evidence point: 1 of ~32 LLaVA-1.5-7B decoder layers compressed (gate/up/down_proj only), TTNS method, bond_dimension=768, on Colab T4. Healing NOT validated for LLaVA at any bond dimension tried in this run (heal_steps_per_layer=0): at chi=96 (mps or ttns, 4 layers, OLD non-sequential script) the compressed model was already near-random before healing even started; at chi=768 with 4 layers compressed simultaneously (also the old script), per-layer relative error (~0.6-0.77) compounded across layers into a forward-pass NaN (fp16 overflow through the residual stream) BEFORE healing could run. The script was since restructured to compress-and-heal ONE layer at a time (GPTQ/AWQ-style sequential calibration) specifically to fix this — see scripts/compress_llava_colab.py docstring — but that fix has not yet been re-run for real on Colab as of this file. The 4-layer target was abandoned as disproportionate additional Colab time for optional evidence. This 1-layer point meets the common compression target: ratio 3.70x (>= 2x threshold) at a 1.9% perplexity increase (<= 5% threshold) on the built-in smoke-test text set (not a real held-out benchmark split).
